messages:
jess: Heads up — we just saw two OOMs on host gpu-rc-13 while serving long chats to model 'redwood/gpt-long-32k' (~2x normal mem). Stack from the kube node shows KV pageflip spikes and sustained growth in KV map entries after ~30k tokens.

mike: ugh. Are these the same failure mode as last week's slab thrash? any core/logs? :thinking:

jess: attaching clipped profiler + kernel trace.

jess: ```\n[perf] kv_cache_entries: 1.2M -> 1.9M (30m)
[trace] page_faults/sec spike to 4.8k
[log] evict_loop: processed 0 entries, mem_available low -> retrying\nOOM: killing process redwood-runtime (pid 4219)\n``` 

anika: looks like entries keep being inserted but eviction solver returns nothing because fragmentation prevents contiguous reclaim. Could be the reuse pointer chasing that doesn't see reclaimable segments.

mike: quick mitigation idea: disable continuous batching on that model/route for Dedicated and Hosted for the next 2h. batching seems to amplify tail allocations.

leo: agreed. Also set a soft cap on kv window for that route: `kv.max_active_prefixes=25000` and `kv.eviction_aggressiveness=2` until we have a root cause patch.

jess: I'm pushing a hotfix branch that forces `kv_preemptive_evict=true` when memory pressure > 70%. Will open PR and canary to 5 hosts.

anika: long term we should add kernel-selection heuristics: prefer the sparse-kernel path when fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 AND mean_seq_len > 8k. The dense kernel is faster but refuses to free small shards.

mike: another safe fallback: on eviction failure escalate to graceful degrade: respond with short truncated context and mark trace id for re-run. That keeps user-visible latency but avoids hard OOM.

leo: rollout plan: jess will cut release -> canary 5 hosts -> monitor metrics: `kv_fragmentation_ratio`, `kv_eviction_failures`, `prefetch_pageflip_rate`. If no regressions for 30m then 25% -> 100% over 2h.

infra-bot: deploy started: pr/4872 -> canary-group (gpu-rc-13, gpu-rc-14, gpu-rc-15, gpu-rc-16, gpu-rc-17). Notify @oncall if kv_eviction_failures > 10/min.

jess: added two extra signals to telemetry: tag traces where we truncated context due to mem-pressure and emit sample prompt + kv sizes (anonymized). Will also stash a small repro harness.

anika: follow-up action items: 1) reproduce locally with long synthetic prefix churn 2) instrument reuse pointer scan to report examined vs reclaimed counts 3) add unit test for kernel selection under fragmentation scenario.

mike: I can own the canary monitor dashboard: I'll create quick panel for eviction latency + reclaim success ratio.

leo: if the hotfix doesn't hold, fallback to model-variant routing: serve longctx requests to quantized-8bit variant with independent cache (less memory) and set circuit-breaker to 5% failure budget.

jess: thanks team. I'm leaving the PR link in the incident ticket and will update when canary metrics show stability. For now, batching off + preemptive eviction + short kv cap are live.

mike: :thumbsup: let's also add a postmortem note if we confirm fragmentation/regression from kernel selection change. please annotate suspected commit hash in the ticket.

leo: noted. I'll coordinate the canary rollback policy if we see latency regressions.

infra-bot: canary completed: 5/5 healthy, kv_eviction_failures trending down. Rolling to 25% now.
